name: shape-on-grid
title: Shape on a centimetre grid
tagline: One rectangle, triangle or parallelogram on centimetre squared paper; sides, area, perimeter derived and occludable; drag-to-construct a shape obeying length/area/perimeter rules.
description: A single named-type shape — a rectangle, a triangle or a parallelogram — drawn on centimetre squared paper (1 square = 1 cm) with its vertices on grid intersections, its dimensions countable on the grid. You write the grid size, a semantic shape (its type and dimensions — width and height for a rectangle, base and perpendicular height for a triangle or parallelogram), and/or the constraints the drawing must satisfy. The model derives everything else: the vertices (always integer grid points), the dimension labels, the perpendicular-height line with its right-angle mark, the area and perimeter (computed by the shoelace rule, so the area is always exact — an integer or half-integer), and — for a marked question — the deterministic wrong start the pupil adjusts plus the canonical correct instance the answer reveals. Occlude the dimension labels, the area or the perimeter for a "work it out" question; highlight the answer readout in amber. Turn a question into a MARKED construct by setting construct: true and hosting the tile with responseMode "construct" and correctAnswer { derived: true }: the pupil is shown a wrong shape of the right type and drags its vertices (snapping to grid intersections) until it obeys the constraints. Marking is position- and orientation-invariant — length is the longer side and width the shorter, so a tall or a wide rectangle both pass, as does any triangle orientation or either parallelogram shear. There are NO live area/perimeter readouts while dragging (that would pre-answer "draw a rectangle with area 40 cm²"); the sides stay countable on the paper, which is the point. Distinct from geometry/area-grid (area by counting shaded squares) and geometry/geoboard (polygon properties on a pin board).
whenToUse: Reach for this to draw ONE shape to a rule on a centimetre grid, or to label the dimensions / area / perimeter of a rectangle, triangle or parallelogram whose sides are countable on squared paper — the "draw a rectangle with length twice its width and perimeter 18 cm", "draw a triangle with base 6 cm and area 9 cm²", "work out the area of this parallelogram" family. Set grid: { cols, rows } to the centimetre squared paper (x runs left-to-right, y bottom-to-top, both in whole centimetres); keep it identical across the blocks of one lesson. WORKED / LABELLED figure: give shape — its type and dimensions (rectangle: width, height; triangle / parallelogram: base, height where height is the PERPENDICULAR height; parallelogram also takes slant, the horizontal shear of the top edge; triangle takes apexShift, the horizontal offset of the apex from the base-left, default 0 for a right-angled triangle) and optionally at: [x, y] to place its anchor (bottom-left for a rectangle, base-left otherwise; omit to centre it). The dimension labels, the perpendicular-height line and the area / perimeter are all derived — never author a length or an area. Show the area and/or perimeter with shape.area: { show: true } / shape.perimeter: { show: true }. QUESTION (unmarked): set shape.occludeDims true (every dimension label renders "?"), or shape.area: { show: true, occlude: true } / shape.perimeter: { show: true, occlude: true } for "what is the area / perimeter?"; the shape stays visible and countable. ANSWER SPACE: omit shape entirely for a blank sheet, and put the task in caption ("Draw a rectangle with an area of 12 cm²."). MARKED construct question ("draw the shape and auto-mark it"): give constraints and set construct: true, then host the model on a marked tile with responseMode "construct" and correctAnswer { derived: true }. Each constraint is either a measure equal to a CONSTANT ({ measure: "perimeter", equals: 18 }) or a measure equal to k times ANOTHER measure ({ measure: "length", equals: { times: 2, of: "width" } }); the measure vocabulary is width / length (rectangle — length is DEFINED as the longer dimension and width the shorter, which is what makes marking orientation-invariant), base / height (triangle & parallelogram; height is the perpendicular height), area and perimeter. Give the shape TYPE via shape: { type: "rectangle" } (dimensions are optional in a construct question — the model derives a canonical answer for the reveal). The pupil sees a wrong shape of that type and drags it into shape; each constraint becomes one marked cell; the verdict is correct only when EVERY constraint holds (within tolerance, default a hair — grid drags land on exact measures; widen tolerance only for deliberately tilted work). Keep the arithmetic / method as block text or a staged explanation, never on the figure. Common configurations: draw-to-a-rule rectangle — constraints [{ measure: "length", equals: { times: 2, of: "width" } }, { measure: "perimeter", equals: 18 }]; draw-a-triangle — [{ measure: "base", equals: { times: 2, of: "height" } }, { measure: "area", equals: 9 }]; single loose rule (many right answers) — one constraint like [{ measure: "area", equals: 24 }]. Switch model when the teaching changes: for area by COUNTING squares (including half-squares) use geometry/area-grid; for the properties of a polygon (equal sides, parallel sides, right angles) on a pin board use geometry/geoboard; for coordinates and plotting points use graphing/coordinate-grid; for a compound / composite area split into rectangles use geometry/compound-area. Synonyms a teacher might use: draw a rectangle, draw a triangle, draw a parallelogram, centimetre grid, squared paper, cm grid, length and width, base and height, perpendicular height, area, perimeter, draw a shape with, construct a shape, dimensions.

grid.description: The centimetre squared paper. 1 square = 1 cm; x runs 0…cols left-to-right, y runs 0…rows bottom-to-top. Vertices sit on the integer intersections. Keep it identical across the blocks of one lesson.

cols.description: Squares ACROSS the paper (x from 0 to cols).

rows.description: Squares UP the paper (y from 0 to rows).

shape.description: The shape to draw — its TYPE and dimensions. Omit entirely for a blank answer space. In a marked construct question the dimensions are optional (only the type is needed — the model derives a canonical answer for the reveal). Vertices are computed from these semantic dimensions and always land on grid intersections; never author a vertex or a length label.

type.description: Which shape. "rectangle" is axis-aligned (width across, height up). "triangle" sits on a horizontal base with its apex above it. "parallelogram" sits on a horizontal base with the top edge sheared sideways.

at.description: Anchor grid point [x, y]: the BOTTOM-LEFT corner of a rectangle, or the LEFT end of the base for a triangle / parallelogram. Omit to centre the shape on the grid.

width.description: Rectangle only: the horizontal side length, in cm.

height.description: The vertical extent, in cm. For a rectangle it is the up side; for a triangle / parallelogram it is the PERPENDICULAR height (apex / top edge sits this many cm above the base).

base.description: Triangle / parallelogram only: the horizontal base length, in cm.

slant.description: Parallelogram only: the horizontal shear of the top edge relative to the base, in cm (the top edge is base-parallel and congruent, shifted this far right; negative shears left). Default 2. 0 would draw a rectangle.

apexShift.description: Triangle only: the horizontal offset of the apex from the base-left end, in cm. Default 0 (a right-angled triangle with the right angle at the base-left). Set to base/2 for an isosceles triangle.

label.description: A name drawn at the shape's centre — "A", "R", or a word. The TEXT is authored (a name cannot be derived); its position is computed. Omit for an unlabelled shape.

occludeDims.description: Render every dimension label ("6 cm", the base, the height) as "?" — the "work out the dimensions" hook. The shape stays visible and countable. Default false.

highlight.description: Draw the shape in amber — emphasis / "this is the answer". Reserved colour; use sparingly. Default false.

area.description: The area readout beneath the figure ("Area = 18 cm²"). Derived; omit the object for no area line.

show.description: Show the derived area readout. Default false.

occlude.description: Render the area value as "?" — "what is the area?". Default false.

highlight.description: Amber the area value — answer emphasis. Default false.

perimeter.description: The perimeter readout beneath the figure ("Perimeter = 18 cm"). Derived; omit the object for no perimeter line.

show.description: Show the derived perimeter readout. Default false.

occlude.description: Render the perimeter value as "?". Default false.

highlight.description: Amber the perimeter value. Default false.

constraints.description: The rules a MARKED construct drawing must satisfy — the marking key (each becomes one graded cell). Only meaningful with construct: true. Two forms only: a measure equal to a CONSTANT, or a measure equal to k times ANOTHER measure. Measure vocabulary: "width"/"length" (rectangle — length is the LONGER side, width the shorter, so marking is orientation-invariant), "base"/"height" (triangle & parallelogram; height is the perpendicular height), "area", "perimeter".

id.description: Optional stable id for this constraint's marked cell (kebab-case). Defaults to c1, c2, … in order.

measure.description: The measure this rule constrains (the left-hand side).

equals.description: The right-hand side: either a NUMBER (measure equals that constant, e.g. perimeter equals 18) OR an object { times, of } (measure equals times × the "of" measure, e.g. length equals 2 × width).

oneOf.description: A constant the measure must equal (in cm, cm² or cm as appropriate).

construct.description: Arm the construction QUESTION state (validator-required when the tile uses responseMode "construct"). The pupil is shown a WRONG shape of the given type and drags its vertices — snapping to grid intersections, the type enforced — until it obeys every constraint. The correct answer is never rendered: each constraint is checked at marking time against the measure the model derives from the vertices (host with correctAnswer { derived: true }). On web the shape follows the drag with amber handles; print and static slides show the same wrong start (no live readouts). Needs a shape.type and at least one constraint. Default false.

start.description: Construct mode only: authored dimensions for the pre-placed WRONG start shape (same dimension fields as shape — width/height or base/height/slant/apexShift, and at). Omit to let the model derive a deterministic wrong start from the constraints. If an authored start happens to satisfy every constraint it is perturbed so the pupil always has something to fix.

at.description: Anchor grid point for the wrong start.

tolerance.description: Construct mode only: the acceptance allowance on each measure (a constraint holds when its two sides are within this of each other, in the measure's units). Default 0.05 — grid drags land on exact whole-cm measures, so keep it tiny; widen only when the answer is deliberately tilted (irrational side lengths).

dims.description: Draw the dimension labels on a worked / labelled figure (length, width, base, perpendicular height). Default true. (Ignored in a construct question — no live readouts there.)

grid.description: Draw the centimetre squared-paper grid. Default true.

unitHint.description: Draw a discreet "1 cm" bracket on one grid square so the scale is explicit. Default false.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the figure; the top padding grows to clear it.

caption.description: Optional line centred below the figure, e.g. a short context note. Never the question or an instruction: that wording is the block's text.

examples.label: Worked example — a 6 cm by 3 cm rectangle with its dimensions, area and perimeter
Blank answer space — an empty centimetre grid to draw on
Occluded question — find the area of this rectangle (dimensions and area hidden)
Hard case — a sheared parallelogram, base 6 cm and perpendicular height 3 cm, area shown

params.caption: The height is the perpendicular distance between the base and the top — not the sloping side.
